title: Process & CLI
lede: What a CLI tool or containerized service needs day-to-day: argv, environment, exit codes, stdin, signals, timing, and child processes. Two recurring divergences: an out-of-range process.argv[i] reads "" (falsy), not Node's undefined; and every event/handler API here takes one listener slot per event, an arrow/function-literal only, firing synchronously from the event loop's dispatch rather than through a microtask queue. child_process (spawn/exec/fork/spawnSync) lives here too — it is what a process orchestrator actually reaches for.

entries.name: process.argv
entries.description: The command-line arguments.
entries.snippet:
const args: string[] = process.argv
for (const a of args) console.log(a)
differences: Mirrors C's `argv` directly (`argv[0]` is the binary's own path), not Node's two-prefix convention.
An out-of-range `process.argv[i]` read yields `""` (falsy), not Node's `undefined` and not the general array bounds throw.

entries.name: process.env
entries.description: Environment variables, via both dot and bracket notation. Returns a possibly-null string (same convention as .find()), so process.env.X ?? "default" works.

returns.desc: The value, or null if unset.

entries.snippet: const path: string = process.env.PATH ?? "no PATH set"

entries.name: process.exit(code)
entries.description: Exits the process. Calls C exit(); never returns, and code after it is correctly unreachable. With no argument, uses process.exitCode.

entries.name: process.readLineSync()
entries.description: Reads one line from stdin via POSIX getline() (handles arbitrarily long lines), stripped of its trailing newline. Returns null at EOF (same possibly-null convention as process.env). The blocking counterpart to the streamed process.stdin and the readline module.

returns.desc: The line, or null at EOF.

entries.snippet:
const line = process.readLineSync()
if (line === null) console.log("no input")

entries.name: Synchronous file read/write
entries.description: Config, data, and log I/O for a CLI program — the full sync/async/stream fs surface has its own reference page.

entries.name: process.execFileSync(file, args?)
entries.description: Node's child_process.execFileSync (not execSync): fork()+execvp()s file directly with no shell, so shell metacharacters in args are never interpreted. Returns captured stdout as a string; throws a catchable Error on a non-zero exit status or a signal death.
differences: No options object (no `cwd`/`env`/`timeout`/`stdio` overrides yet).
stderr is inherited (visible on the terminal live), not captured.

entries.name: process.cwd()
entries.description: The current working directory, via POSIX getcwd(NULL, 0) (auto-sizing).

entries.name: process.chdir(path)
entries.description: Changes the current working directory via POSIX chdir(). Throws a catchable Error (the same shape fs.*'s failures use) if the path doesn't exist or isn't a directory.

entries.name: process.pid
entries.description: The current process ID, via POSIX getpid(). A property read, not a call.

entries.name: process.platform
entries.description: A pure compile-time constant ("darwin"/"linux"/"win32"/…) baked in from the Go compiler's runtime.GOOS — no runtime code, since this compiler doesn't cross-compile.

entries.name: process.arch
entries.description: A compile-time constant ("arm64"/"x64"/…) from the Go compiler's runtime.GOARCH, exactly like process.platform.

entries.name: process.execPath
entries.description: The absolute, symlink-resolved path of the running executable — the compiled program is itself the binary (no separate runtime). Always absolute like Node's, not a raw argv[0].

entries.name: process.emitWarning(message, type?)
entries.description: Writes (node:<pid>) <type>: <message> to stderr, type defaulting to "Warning", and (like Node's always-on default printer) additionally invokes any process.on('warning', …) listener with the warning as an Error.
differences: No options-object form (`{ code, detail }`) and no first-warning `--trace-warnings` hint line.

entries.name: process.kill(pid, signal?)
entries.description: Sends signal (defaults to 15/SIGTERM, matching real Node) to pid via POSIX kill(). Throws a catchable Error if the target doesn't exist or the signal can't be sent; signal 0 is the standard POSIX existence check and delivers nothing.

entries.name: process.stdout.write / stderr.write
entries.signature: process.stdout.write(s: string): void; process.stderr.write(s: string): void
entries.description: A raw write of exactly s with nothing appended — unlike console.log/.error's always-trailing newline. Useful for a progress indicator or assembling one line from pieces. stdout is buffered (fd 1, ordering-correct against console.log); stderr is unbuffered (fd 2).
differences: Text-only (byte-string, not binary-safe past an embedded null — the same scope narrowing `console.log` has).
Beyond `.write` and `.isTTY` (a real `isatty(fd)` probe), `process.stdout`/`stderr` expose no other stream surface (no `.columns`/`.rows`, no `'drain'`).

entries.name: Writing process.env
entries.description: Sets an environment variable via setenv(key, String(val), overwrite); a written variable is inherited by child processes.
differences: Write only — no `delete process.env.KEY` (`delete` is not a parser keyword; the fixed-shape object model has no dynamic delete).
Compound assignment (`process.env.X += …`) is a clean rejection.

entries.name: process.on('SIGINT'/'SIGTERM', handler)
entries.description: Lets a running program (e.g. an http.listen server) intercept a signal and shut down gracefully instead of dying immediately.
differences: The handler runs from ordinary control flow at the top of the event loop's iteration, never from real async signal context.
Event name must be a compile-time string literal, exactly `'SIGINT'`/`'SIGTERM'`.
Handler must be a zero-argument `() => void` closure; one handler slot per signal (re-registering overwrites).
Only fires while a `http.listen`- or timer-driven event loop is actively iterating; a plain synchronous script has no loop to check from.

entries.name: process.on('exit'/'uncaughtException'/'warning') + exitCode
entries.description: 'exit' fires at normal end and from process.exit(), receiving the exit code; process.exitCode = N sets the deferred code a bare program returns; process.exit() with no argument uses it.
entries.snippet:
process.on('exit', (code: number) => console.log("exiting with code", code))
process.exitCode = 0
differences: `'uncaughtException'` runs the listener (suppressing the default print) but the process still exits (code 1) — the setjmp/longjmp model has already unwound to the top-level catch, so it can't resume like Node.
No `'unhandledRejection'` yet (needs rejected-promise tracking).
One listener slot per event, arrow-literal only.

entries.name: process.hrtime() / .bigint()
entries.description: CLOCK_MONOTONIC high-resolution timing. hrtime() returns a [seconds, nanoseconds] tuple, .bigint() total-nanoseconds as a bigint.
entries.snippet:
const start = process.hrtime.bigint()
const elapsed = process.hrtime.bigint() - start
differences: `hrtime()` takes no argument — the legacy diff-from-a-previous-reading form isn't supported (use `.bigint()` and subtract).

entries.name: process.getuid() / geteuid() / getgid() / getegid()
entries.description: Direct POSIX credential reads returning a number — present unconditionally (this compiler is POSIX-only), matching Node-on-POSIX.

entries.name: process.memoryUsage()
entries.signature: process.memoryUsage(): { rss: number; heapTotal: number; heapUsed: number; external: number; arrayBuffers: number }
entries.description: Returns Node's object shape. Only rss carries a real value — the process's peak resident set size, read from getrusage(2)'s ru_maxrss (bytes on macOS, kilobytes scaled on Linux). There is no managed V8 heap to measure in a native build, so heapTotal/heapUsed/external/arrayBuffers are returned as 0 rather than fabricated, and rss is peak rather than the instantaneous value Node reports.

returns.desc: Memory-usage byte counts; only rss is populated.

caveats: rss is peak resident set (ru_maxrss), not the live value

entries.name: process.nextTick(fn)
entries.description: Enqueues fn on the existing microtask queue.
differences: Shares the one microtask FIFO with Promise reactions rather than draining strictly before them (Node keeps a separate nextTick queue ahead of promises); zero-argument `() => void` callback only.

entries.name: process.version / process.versions
entries.description: process.version = "v22.11.0"; process.versions is a real object (JSON.stringify/field access/Object.keys all work), matching Node v22.11.0's node/v8 verbatim, plus a klain key for this compiler's version.
differences: `versions` reports only honest values — `node`/`v8`/`klain` — deliberately omitting bundled-lib keys this compiler doesn't ship (`uv`/`undici`/`icu`/…) rather than fabricate them.
The real linked-library versions (`openssl`/`zlib`) are a follow-on — they need a runtime lib query.
`node`/`v8` track the compatibility *ceiling* (the pinned test-corpus release); a `--node-compat` floor is deferred.

entries.name: process.uptime()
entries.description: Seconds (a double) since process start, captured once at main entry via CLOCK_MONOTONIC.

entries.name: process.stdin (streamed)
entries.description: Streamed stdin over a non-blocking fd 0 folded into the same select() loop as readline/child_process: 'data' per read chunk, 'end' once on EOF. Distinct from the blocking readLineSync() and the line-oriented readline module.
differences: `'data'` delivers each chunk as a UTF-8 string, not a `Buffer` — no `setEncoding`, no binary mode.
Flowing mode only (attaching `'data'` starts it) — no `.pause()`/`.resume()`/`.read()`/`'readable'`.
One listener per event, arrow/function-expression literal only; callbacks fire synchronously from the dispatch, not via a microtask.

entries.name: readline module
entries.signature: readline.createInterface({ input }); rl.on('line' | 'close'); rl.question(q, cb); rl.close()
entries.description: Line-oriented stdin over the same non-blocking select() loop as child_process: one 'line' per newline (CR stripped), an unterminated final line flushed on EOF, then 'close'. Distinct from the blocking readLineSync().
differences: Listener callbacks fire synchronously from the event loop's dispatch, not deferred through a microtask queue.
One listener per event, an arrow/function-expression literal only; no line history/editing, no `SIGINT`/`'pause'`/`'resume'`, no completer.
The `createInterface` options object is accepted but ignored — input is always stdin, output always stdout; one active interface at a time.

entries.name: child_process.spawn / exec / execFile (async)
entries.signature: spawn(cmd, args?, opts?); exec(cmd, cb); execFile(file, args?, cb)
entries.description: fork()+execvp() with three pipes; the read ends are non-blocking and fold into the same select() event loop as Worker/channel pipes. spawn streams (child.stdout/stderr 'data'/'end', child.on('close'/'exit'), child.stdin.write/.end, child.pid, child.kill); exec runs via /bin/sh -c and execFile execvp's directly, both buffering into one (err, stdout, stderr) callback.
differences: Listener callbacks fire synchronously from the event loop's dispatch, not deferred through the microtask queue.
One listener per event, an arrow/function-expression literal only; no `removeListener`.

spawn's options support `{ cwd, shell, stdio: 'pipe' }` — `cwd` is real, `shell` is accepted but **ignored** (commands always exec directly), and `env`/`detached`/stdio arrays are clean rejections; exec/execFile take no options.
`'close'`/`'exit'` receive the exit `code` only (a signal death folds to `128+signal`).
Handles and their buffered output are never freed (`-mm=manual`).

entries.name: child_process.fork (self-fork + IPC)
entries.description: Node's own mechanism: socketpair + re-exec of the current binary with NODE_CHANNEL_FD set; NDJSON string frames. Parent: child.send(str)→bool, child.on('message'/'exit'/'close'), child.disconnect(); child: process.send(str)→bool, process.on('message'), process.disconnect().

returns.desc: The forked child with an IPC channel.

differences: Self-fork only: the path must be `__filename` or `process.argv[1]` (forking a *different* module is a clean rejection); the options object must be an empty `{}`.
Messages are strings (`send(obj)` is a clean rejection); one `'message'` listener per side.
Bare `process.send` reads as a *boolean* forked-ness probe, not Node's function-or-undefined.
`process.argv[i]` out-of-range reads yield `""` (falsy) rather than Node's `undefined`.

entries.name: child_process.spawnSync / execSync / execFileSync
entries.signature: spawnSync(cmd, args?, opts?); execSync(cmd); execFileSync(file, args?)
entries.description: One embedded C core: fork + execvp with both stdio pipes poll-multiplexed to completion (no deadlock when a child fills stderr while stdout drains), then a blocking waitpid; execSync runs via /bin/sh -c. Distinct from the bespoke process.execFileSync above.
differences: Options object supports `{ cwd, encoding: 'utf8' }` only (no `env`/`timeout`/`input`/`shell`/`stdio`); results are strings, not Buffers.
`spawnSync`'s result carries `status`/`stdout`/`stderr`/`pid` only — no `signal`/`error`/`output` fields (a signal death folds into `status` as `128+signal`).
`execSync`/`execFileSync` return stdout but do **not** throw on a non-zero exit status (Node throws) — use `spawnSync().status` where the exit code matters.
